items.narrative:
This audit covers 761 traceability events recorded between 2025-01-03 and 2025-09-23, spanning 32 products all of which fall into the definite_on tier of the Food Traceability List. Across those events, 551 are shipping, 145 are transformation, 64 are first land-based receiving, and 1 is receiving. The business transacts with 29 external trading partners, all rated Band A, and logged 216 internal transfer events with 0 unknown-destination events during the period.

The audit surfaced 15 findings in total — 5 rated high severity and 10 rated medium. The most pressing issues are the 5 high-severity findings, which include a traceability plan gap, scope or exemption uncertainty on 2 products, and lot-integrity problems that together flag 41 duplicate TLC records, 6 backward-lineage lots needing review, 1 mass-balance anomaly, 1 self-receive anomaly, and 1 transformation-linkage anomaly. KDE completeness is strong at a 96.92% coverage rate, but 209 of 6,785 graded KDE fields are still missing. Two products — IDs 04598767000211 and 04598767000495 — are declared as General products in the system yet score as definite_on for the Food Traceability List, creating a direct compliance misclassification risk.

The immediate priorities are: first, resolve the traceability plan finding and the 2 scope-or-exemption-uncertainty findings before any regulatory review, as these are high-severity and foundational; second, reclassify products 04598767000211 and 04598767000495 from General products to the correct Food Traceability List category in the Product Master; third, work through the 41 duplicate TLC records and the 6 backward-lineage lots flagged as needs_review in the lot-integrity module, then address the single date-ordering, mass-balance, self-receive, and transformation-linkage anomalies in sequence; finally, locate and populate the 209 missing KDE fields to close the gap between the current 96.92% rate and full coverage.
